reasoning: Both attempts fix all four bugs the same way: copy-on-write history, a fresh table in clear, useSignalState for the Last label, and a cleanup-wrapped subscribe on the count. A also turns getLastPlaced into a computed over history, which is a cleaner design but a larger change to the store. B keeps the original structure and batches the two setter calls. B wins narrowly on minimal, scoped change; otherwise the two are nearly equal.

criteria.note: onBlockPlaced uses setHistory(function(history) local nextHistory = table.clone(history) ... return nextHistory end); no frozen flag or trigger.
Vide.cleanup(Charm.subscribe(PlacedBlocks.getCount, ...)) ties the subscription to the HUD scope.
Replaces the lastPlaced signal with a Charm.computed over history; the public API still works, but the store is restructured beyond the minimal fix.
luau-lsp, selene and StyLua all pass.
setHistory updater clones history, inserts, and returns the new table; no frozen or trigger workaround.
lastPlaced = VideCharm.useSignalState(PlacedBlocks.getLastPlaced) bound in the label's Text.
cleanup(Charm.subscribe(PlacedBlocks.getCount, ...)) disposes the subscription when show tears the HUD down.
Keeps the store's structure and API, and adds Charm.batch so both signals update together.
luau-lsp, selene and StyLua all pass.

strengths: Single source of truth: last placed is derived from history
Clear comments explaining the immutability and the scope cleanup
weaknesses: Restructures the store (drops the lastPlaced signal), more change than strictly needed

strengths: Minimal, targeted fixes that keep the original store design
Uses batch so the two signals update atomically
weaknesses: Keeps two signals that could in principle drift apart (mitigated by batch)
